sentences.text:
Respondent :- Dabbu @ Anurudh
Counsel for Appellant :- G.A.
Hon'ble Siddharth,J.
Order on Leave to Appeal Application Heard Sri G.N. Kanaujia, learned A.G.A-I for the State and
perused the record.
Learned A.G.A-I has submitted that from the FIR and the evidence on record, it was clear that the respondent committed the offence of rape against a minor girl aged about 10 years forcefully.
The medical evidence fully corroborated the prosecution case.
The statement of witnesses including the victim was quite clear and therefore the conviction of the respondent under Section 376(2), 506 IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act only was unwarranted.
The acquittal of the respondent for committing the offence under Section 3(2)(v) and Section 3(1)(w) of SC/ST Act was also unwarranted.

sentences.text: He has further submitted that the medical evidence clearly proved the prosecution case but the trial court has not punished the respondent under Section 376AB IPC when the case for punishment under the aforesaid sections was fully proved from the material on record.
The application for leave to appeal is allowed.
Issue bailable warrant through CJM, Etawah to the respondent.

CJM, Etawah, who shall enlarge the respondent on bail on furnishing personal bond of Rs. 20,000/- and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of C.J.M., Etawah with the undertaking that they shall appear before this court as and when required.
Lower court record has been received.
As soon as personal and surety bonds are furnished photocopies of the same are directed to be transmitted to this court forthwith by the concerned court to be kept on record.
Office is directed to get the paper books prepared within six weeks.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The medical evidence fully corroborated the prosecution case.
The statement of witnesses including the victim was quite clear and therefore the conviction of the respondent under Section 376(2), 506 IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act only was unwarranted.
The acquittal of the respondent for committing the offence under Section 3(2)(v) and Section 3(1)(w) of SC/ST Act was also unwarranted.
He has further submitted that the medical evidence clearly proved the prosecution case but the trial court has not punished the respondent under Section 376AB IPC when the case for punishment under the aforesaid sections was fully proved from the material on record.
